title: SPORTS LOVERS
subtitle: For questions 1–8, read the text below and think of the word which best fits each gap. Use only one word in each gap. There is an example at the beginning (0).
passage:
Some people seem to love the challenge of extreme sports. They enjoy the adrenaline rush (0) that breaks up the boredom of everyday life. It would be easy to regard these daredevils [[1]] dangerous and irresponsible. In actual [[2]], there is often much less risk involved than you'd think.

As [[3]] as possible, very little is left to chance. Professional base jumpers have been known to turn back when conditions haven't been right, even [[4]] this has meant letting down a film crew. If the jumpers don't feel safe jumping, nothing will happen [[5]] they are ready.

This is [[6]] to the fact that there isn't a rule book for extreme sports professionals. They're writing it as they go along. [[7]] a mistake could have very serious consequences. This leads [[8]] a sense of trust, both in yourself and in your environment, which isn't encouraged in modern life. We are too worried about what could go wrong.

explanations.1: **Regard … as** — fixed pattern: see or treat someone as something.
explanations.2: **In actual fact** — set phrase meaning ‘really’ or ‘in reality’.
explanations.3: **As far as possible** — to the greatest extent they can; minimal chance-taking.
explanations.4: **Even if** — concession: they turned back despite disappointing the crew.
explanations.5: **Until** — nothing happens before the moment they feel ready.
explanations.6: **Due to the fact that** — standard linker introducing the reason.
explanations.7: **As / Because / Since** — reason clause: mistakes in extreme sports can be fatal.
explanations.8: **Leads to** — fixed collocation: results in a sense of trust.
